rationale: Jesus names Solomon and describes a royal visitor: "The Queen of the South will rise at the judgment with this generation and condemn it; for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon" (12:42, BSB). 1 Kings 10:1-13 narrates that visit: "when the queen of Sheba heard about the fame of Solomon... she came to test him with difficult questions," and "saw all the wisdom of Solomon" (10:1, 10:4, BSB). A script over the shipped BSB finds "queen of Sheba" only in 1 Kings 10 and its parallel, 2 Chronicles 9:1-12, and "Queen of the South" only in Matthew 12:42 and Luke 11:31. Matthew Henry and MacLaren (via Biblehub) both name her the queen of Sheba. The title is the one real difference: the Greek has basilissa notou, "queen of the south," where the Septuagint has basilissa Saba, and "from the ends of the earth" is Matthew's phrase, not 1 Kings'. Graded explicit_reference at explicit, like conn-matt12-nineveh-jonah3, because Solomon is named and only one such visit is narrated in the Old Testament; 2 Chronicles 9 is not authored as a separate row.
